messages:
marta: RFC follow-up: proposing an explicit admission/gating layer for runtime lanes so we can control fairness and per-tenant burst behavior. not a router replacement, more like an admission controller that annotates requests with lane decisions and enforcement tokens. looking for concerns before I write the addendum.

omar: sounds useful. quick Q: will admission be synchronous (block until decision) or async (token bucket check then proceed)?

marta: plan is synchronous lightweight check (<1ms) that returns either admission token or a retry-after hint. heavy decisions (costly checks) should be cached.

kevin: cache implications: admission decisions should include a "cache_hint" so downstream cache layers can decide whether to warm or not. otherwise we'll thrash hot caches.

anjali: telemetry + billing: every admission decision must emit a trace with reason code (admitted, throttled, fallback, lane-mismatch). also tag usage billing events with lane and decision for accurate cost allocation.

sam: fairness: need per-tenant slow-start windows and an inter-tenant floor so noisy tenants cannot monopolize fastpath. propose leaky-bucket + decay window and a separate reserved quota for critical tenants.

marta: agreed. propose policy primitives: per-tenant rate, burst (tokens), reserved_quota, affinity_score (stickiness), and priority (for paid tiers).

omar: edge cases: retries should not get double advantage. admission tokens should be bound to request id and short-lived. make tokens non-reusable.

kevin: security: admission must validate auth and tenant scoping; if admission is bypassed for internal debug, that should be auditable. also expose an allowlist for dedicated customers to pin to a lane.

anjali: test plan: unit tests for token lifecycle, integration test with simulated tenants (mix of small and noisy), and a canary with 0.5% traffic for 24-48h. add synthetic load that tries to game the bucket.

sam: implementation note: keep admission layer stateless where possible (use sharded counters in redis/gcache) to avoid single-point hotness. also include a local cache for decisions to reduce RPCs.

marta: failure modes: admission service down -> fail-open or fail-closed? my proposal: fail-open to avoid global outage but emit high-severity alert and switch to conservative defaults (very small burst windows).

omar: fail-open is pragmatic but risky. require a kill-switch that ops can flip to fail-closed during attacks. include automated health checks that flip behavior based on downstream latency and error rates.

kevin: compatibility: admission should append headers so legacy components can opt-in later. avoid changing request shape otherwise.

anjali: add monitoring: per-tenant admission rates, throttle rates, lane-change counts, retry-after distribution, and billing deltas. dashboards + alerting thresholds.

sam: action items:
- sam: prototype admission shim + token lifecycle (10d)
- kevin: cache_hint spec + rehydrate signal (5d)
- anjali: telemetry schema + billing hooks (5d)
- marta: short RFC addendum + policy language primitives (3d)

deploy-bot: noted. will create a canary checklist that requires the PRs above and a 0.5% canary run for 48h before wider rollout.

marta: thanks. i'll draft the addendum and loop in product for reserved quota definitions. any other risks to call out?

omar: fairness violations, ops complexity, and potential billing confusion. include mitigation steps.

kevin: also add a small A/B test for cache-hit effect when admission routes to economized lanes.

marta: perfect. i'll post the draft RFC addendum by EOD and schedule a quick sync next week.
